title: Fragments
objectives: Explain what fragments are and why they exist
Use the fragment lifecycle and viewLifecycleOwner
Avoid the classic fragment view-leak bug

sections.markdown: A Fragment is a reusable, modular portion of UI hosted inside an Activity (or another Fragment). Fragments enable adaptive layouts (e.g., list + detail on tablets) and modern single-activity navigation.
If an Activity is a window, fragments are interchangeable panes inside it — you can swap, combine, or reuse them without changing the window.

## Two lifecycles
A fragment has its own lifecycle AND a separate **view** lifecycle. The view can be destroyed (e.g., on the back stack) while the fragment instance lives on.

Observing LiveData with the fragment's lifecycle instead of **viewLifecycleOwner** — when the view is recreated you get duplicate observers and crashes/leaks. Always use viewLifecycleOwner in onViewCreated.
Modern apps favor a single Activity + many fragments with the Navigation component, and communicate via a shared ViewModel scoped to the activity or nav graph.

flashcards.front: Why do fragments have two lifecycles?
flashcards.back: The fragment instance can outlive its view (e.g., on the back stack), so the view has its own lifecycle.

flashcards.front: Which owner for LiveData in a fragment?
flashcards.back: viewLifecycleOwner — so observers are tied to the view, not the longer-lived fragment.
Through a ViewModel scoped to the activity or nav graph.

quiz.q: A fragment must be hosted by…
quiz.explain: Fragments live inside a host (Activity or parent Fragment).

quiz.q: To observe LiveData in a fragment, use…
quiz.explain: viewLifecycleOwner prevents duplicate observers when the view is recreated.
Single-activity architecture with the Navigation component is the recommended pattern.

challenges.text: Host two fragments in one activity and swap them with a FragmentTransaction.
Share state between fragments via an activity-scoped ViewModel.
Build a master-detail layout that adapts between phone and tablet.
Reproduce and fix a fragment view leak by switching to viewLifecycleOwner.
